title: Expanding tiles on a small screen and when it can't expand
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in as an owner/admin (or any user with the Reports permission) on the build under test; a single workplace is selected.
  2. A small screen (browser window under 1024px).
custom_steps:
1. Confirm there is no 'expand all' / 'collapse all' control and no Panel-versus-Inline view choice.
2. On a small screen, confirm a tile cannot be expanded in place; in place of 'View details' the footer is a 'View Report' link that opens the tile's full report.
3. On a small screen, confirm the At Risk Customers tile shows no footer link (no report) and its detail table is reachable only on a desktop screen.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • The dashboard has no "expand all" or "collapse all" control.
  • The dashboard has no Panel-versus-Inline view choice.
  • On a small screen, a tile cannot be expanded in place.
  • On a small screen, in place of "View details", the tile's footer is a "View Report" link that opens the tile's full report.
  • On a small screen, the At Risk Customers tile shows no footer link (it has no report), and its detail table is reachable only on a desktop screen.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-490, story SV-9578 (S6 — Expanding a Tile); Dashboard v1 specification, Confluence page 788430850, section S6; read on 2 October 2026.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S6-N1: “The dashboard has no "expand all" or "collapse all" control.”
  • S6-N2: “The dashboard has no Panel-versus-Inline view choice.”
  • S6-E1: “On a small screen (see Terminology), a tile cannot be expanded in place.”
  • S6-E2: “On a small screen, in place of the "View details" control, the tile's footer is a "View Report" link that opens the tile's full report.”
  • S6-E3: “On a small screen, the At Risk Customers tile shows no footer link, because it has no report to open (S10-N1); its detail table is reachable only on a desktop screen.”

Last checked against build v26.39.1-09be696 on 10/2/2026.
